- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:503-514 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_filing_lock` may not mutually exclude the detached `report-now` process and the `file` process, allowing races when they read and write shared state.
  WHY: Deepseek rates this BLOCKER and Grok rates it MAJOR; z-ai_glm-5_2 explicitly disagrees, saying `flock` serializes these separate processes.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:672-686 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A reporter reads the last log record instead of the specific prompt that triggered it, so rapid successive events can cause the earlier prompt to be missed.
  WHY: The detached reporter may start after a later event has appended to the same session log, causing it to report the later prompt instead; z-ai_glm-5_2 notes the immediate report is missing even if the prompt is filed later.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:516-635 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Immediate-report deduplication and the report cap use shared state keyed by signature rather than session, so one session can suppress another session's report or consume its cap.
  WHY: The documentation describes per-session limits, while the shared state enforces them across sessions on the same machine and checkout.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py:98-120 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `spawn_reporter` starts a detached reporter for every `PermissionRequest` without a feature flag or kill switch.
  WHY: These reviewers say the behavior cannot be disabled without changing or reverting the hook; z-ai_glm-5_2 disagrees, citing the hook's no-environment-reads invariant and the reporter's existing gates.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:733-770 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: If local state saving fails after a successful GitHub POST, the signature is not recorded and a later attempt can post a duplicate issue comment.
  WHY: The state is persisted after the POST, so a filesystem error can leave subsequent `report-now` or `file` calls believing the report was not filed; the reviewers disagree on severity, with Grok rating it MAJOR and the others that state severity rating it NIT.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: lines 503-514 (_filing_lock function using fcntl.flock()) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The lock mechanism uses fcntl.flock() on file descriptions independently opened by each process. On Linux, flock() locks are associated with the open file description, not the inode. When the detached report-now subprocess (started via subprocess.Popen with start_new_session=True) and the file command (step 14 of the stage session) both independently open filing.lock via Path.open("a"), they each receive a separate open file description. Each process acquires its own independent exclusive lock -- the two locks do not mutually exclude each other.
  WHY: If report-now finishes its POST and writes immediate-state.json between file's read of _load_immediate_state and its later _save_state, file can overwrite the recorded signature. This violates the documented contract that a signature is reported at most once per session. The detached reporter and the stage session are always different processes.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: line 741, _report_now calling _last_record(log_file) to discover which prompt was just logged | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hook does not pass the specific record to the reporter. Instead, the reporter independently reads the last JSON line of the session log by calling _last_record.
  WHY: If two PermissionRequest events fire in rapid succession -- hook event A appends record_A and spawns reporter_A, then hook event B appends record_B and spawns reporter_B before reporter_A has finished starting up -- reporter_A reads record_B (the last line) as its target, computes record_B's signature, and reports it. Record_A is silently dropped and never reported.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py: lines 119-121, spawn_reporter called unconditionally on every PermissionRequest | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hook spawns a detached subprocess on every PermissionRequest with no environment-variable kill switch or feature flag.
  WHY: A broken gh installation or network partition that causes every detached report-now to hang indefinitely would accumulate zombie processes on the runner with no way to stop them short of reverting the hook.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: lines 763-770, POST happens at line 760, then state saves at lines 765-770 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The reporter POSTs to GitHub first, then writes immediate-state.json and filed-state.json. If _save_immediate_state or _save_state raises after the POST succeeded (disk full, permission denied), the outer try/except in report_now returns "error: ..." and the local state is lost.
  WHY: A non-fatal filesystem error between a successful POST and the local save can produce a duplicate comment or issue visible to the operator.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: lines 516-526, _load_immediate_state | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The immediate-state.json deduplication and the 5-report cap are enforced per checkout (the state file lives in the shared log directory ~/.claude/permission-prompts/), not per session.
  WHY: A second session's stuck prompt can be silently skipped because a previous session already reported it. Similarly, a second session can drain the 5-report cap from previous sessions, causing all its later prompts to be silently ignored.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: lines 453-460, _git_output and local_repo_slug signature change | severity=NIT | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: local_repo_slug gained a new optional parameter cwd: str | None = None. The old signature accepted zero arguments; the new one accepts zero or one. All existing zero-argument callers are backward-compatible because the parameter defaults to None.
  WHY: No in-repo runtime failure. The optional default keeps existing call sites working. Only worth flagging because the helper is publicly exported by name from permission_prompts.py and a downstream consumer script that monkey-patched the old zero-arg form or relied on inspect.signature could notice.
- Requirement: "tests/test_permission_prompts.py: 85 passed, 36 of them new" (PR description)
  Expected change site: tests/test_permission_prompts.py
  Evidence of absence: The diff shows 35+ new test functions present in tests/test_permission_prompts.py. Every test named in the PR description is visible in the diff including the immediate-report tests, hook-spawn tests, lookup tests, session-meta tests, contract tests, and the test_hook_has_no_api_calls_or_env_reads narrowing. This requirement is fulfilled.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: 503–514, `_filing_lock` | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `_filing_lock` context manager uses `fcntl.flock()` on independently opened file descriptions, which provides no mutual exclusion between the detached `report-now` process and the `file` process called by step 14.
  WHY: On Linux, `flock()` locks are associated with the open file description, not the inode. When `report-now` and `file` each call `(log_dir / LOCK_FILE).open("a")`, they get separate open file descriptions. Both processes can acquire an exclusive flock on their own file descriptor simultaneously. They race on reading/writing `immediate-state.json` and `filed-state.json`, potentially causing lost report records, duplicate GitHub issues, or corrupted state files.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: 669–685, `_last_record` | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The reporter child `report-now` reads the log file and takes the last record as the prompt it was spawned for.
  WHY: If multiple `PermissionRequest` events arrive rapidly, hook A appends record A and spawns reporter A; hook B appends record B and spawns reporter B. If reporter A starts slowly, it may read the file after hook B has appended record B. Reporter A will report record B, and record A will be missed or reported twice.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: 516–525 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The dedup signature (once per session) and the 5-report cap are enforced globally per checkout directory, not per session.
  WHY: The documentation states these are per-session guarantees ("once per session", "at most 5 per session"), but the implementation uses immediate-state.json shared by all sessions on the same machine and checkout. If two Claude Code sessions encounter the same prompt signature, the second session's prompt is silently skipped, violating the per-session contract.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: 503–514 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `filing.lock` is opened in append mode ("a") and is never truncated or cleaned up.
  WHY: The file grows indefinitely across sessions. While not a crash risk (it is only used for advisory locking), it is an unbounded-growth pattern.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py: 98–109, `spawn_reporter` | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `spawn_reporter` starts a detached reporter on every `PermissionRequest` without an env-var kill switch or feature flag.
  WHY: This introduces a new, detached background process that cannot be disabled without reverting the hook file. If the reporter triggers production issues (e.g., hanging, resource leaks, excessive API calls), maintainers cannot quickly disable it via repository variables or env vars.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
